question: A mother who follows a strict vegan diet is exclusively breastfeeding her infant. Laboratory evaluation of the infant reveals a high MCV (macrocytosis) and hypersegmented neutrophils on a peripheral smear. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these hematologic findings?

answers.option: Decreased maternal intake of Vitamin B12
Decreased maternal intake of folic acid

question: A 5-year-old child presents for a wellness check. The parents report a sedentary lifestyle characterized by frequent fast-food consumption and excessive screen time. Which of the following is the most appropriate tool to assess this child's nutritional status and screen for obesity?

answers.option: Body Mass Index (BMI) for age percentiles

question: A 12-year-old child with a sedentary lifestyle and a diet consisting primarily of junk food is found to have a BMI of 22 kg/m2 (which is high for his age/sex percentile). Both parents have type 2 diabetes, and the child has recently experienced rapid weight gain. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Decrease caloric intake without further testing
Reassurance that the BMI is within a normal adult range
Check HbA1c to screen for type 2 diabetes

question: A child presents with a history of persistent polyuria and polydipsia. Laboratory evaluation reveals a random blood sugar of 110 mg/dL and a serum sodium level of 155 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's clinical presentation?

A 6-month-old infant is diagnosed with West syndrome based on the clinical presentation of infantile spasms and an EEG showing hypsarrhythmia. Which of the following is considered a first-line pharmacological treatment for this condition?

A 14-year-old girl presents with fluctuating ptosis and generalized muscle weakness that worsens toward the end of the day. In the absence of acetylcholine receptor antibody testing, which of the following is the most sensitive electrophysiological test to confirm a diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis?

A 6-month-old boy presents with a history of recurrent diarrheal infections and persistent oral thrush since birth. Laboratory evaluation shows a normal total leukocyte count, but the differential count reveals 90% neutrophils and only 10% lymphocytes (significant lymphopenia). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-day-old infant has not yet passed meconium and presents with progressive abdominal distension and bilious vomiting. A barium enema reveals a microcolon. There is no explosive passage of stool upon digital rectal examination. Given the findings and a positive family history of respiratory issues, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents with a 3-month history of low-grade fever, generalized lymphadenopathy, and significant weight loss. On examination, the child is emaciated and pale, with palpable hepatosplenomegaly. The family history reveals that the grandmother recently died after having similar symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

During a well-child visit, an infant is observed to roll over and sit steadily without support. The infant is also able to transfer a small toy from one hand to the other. At approximately what age are these specific motor and coordinative milestones typically achieved?

A 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department immediately after eating fish at a restaurant. He has developed widespread urticaria, swelling of the lips, and inspiratory stridor. What is the most appropriate first-line pharmacological intervention for this patient?

A 19-year-old male presents with a 4-day history of progressive, symmetric, ascending muscle weakness and absent deep tendon reflexes. He is diagnosed with Guillain-Barré Syndrome. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment to hasten recovery?

A 5-year-old child is brought to the emergency department in the midst of a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that has lasted 20 minutes. answers.option: Immediate intubation and induction of general anesthesia
Give a second dose of IV diazepam (or lorazepam)
Load with IV fosphenytoin or phenobarbital

question: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a 3-day history of high-grade fever, vomiting, and pain in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen. His parents mention that the family recently went on a camping trip where the child drank water from a nearby stream. On physical examination, the child appears ill and has a tender, palpable liver edge 4 cm below the costal margin. Laboratory investigations reveal moderately elevated serum transaminases (AST and ALT). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child with cerebral palsy is evaluated for developmental progress. Clinical observation shows the child has achieved stable head control and can sit with external support, but cannot yet sit independently. The child is also able to transfer objects from one hand to the other. Based on these specific motor and manipulative milestones, what is the child's approximate developmental age?

An infant is born with multiple congenital anomalies including microcephaly, a prominent occiput, micrognathia (small jaw), and low-set malformed ears. Physical examination reveals clenched fists with the index finger overlapping the third finger, and "rocker-bottom" feet. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A child is brought to the clinic with a history of acute diarrhea. On assessment according to IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) guidelines, the child has very sunken eyes and the skin pinch goes back very slowly (more than 2 seconds). The child is lethargic and unable to drink. What is the most appropriate management?

answers.option: Manage with Plan B (Oral Rehydration Therapy in clinic)
Manage with Plan C (IV fluids/Ringer's Lactate) and give Zinc
Give oral antibiotics and send home
Relieve sore throat symptoms and follow up in 2 days

question: A partially vaccinated child presents with a 3-day history of high-grade fever, followed by vomiting and abdominal pain for 2 days. Physical examination reveals a non-blanching macular rash and signs of systemic illness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents with coarse facial features, including a large skull with heavy eyebrows, a broad thick nose, and corneal clouding (opaque corneas). Other findings include a short neck, lumbodorsal kyphosis, hepatosplenomegaly, an umbilical hernia, and broad hands. The child also exhibits significant developmental delay. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old child presents with persistent pain and swelling in the small joints of both hands and feet, specifically involving the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints. On examination, more than five joints are affected symmetrically. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child presents with swollen, painful joints (dactylitis). A sibling has a history of similar complaints. Hemoglobin electrophoresis reveals HbF at 70%, with the remainder being HbA and HbA2​. Notably, the child has never received a blood transfusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with an itchy rash involving the face, scalp, and extremities, but notably sparing the diaper area. The father has a history of allergic rhinitis, and a 5-year-old sibling has similar skin issues. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents with generalized edema (anasarca). Urinalysis reveals 3+ protein but no red cell casts. Laboratory tests show a serum albumin level of less than 2.5 g/dL and mild anemia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

According to the KDIGO clinical practice guidelines for AKI, what is the most likely stage of this injury?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the emergency department one hour after accidentally ingesting half a bottle of paracetamol syrup. The child is currently stable, conscious, and following commands. What is the most appropriate immediate management step for this patient?

A child with a known diagnosis of Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) has been experiencing a persistent fever for one month despite being on various antibiotics. He is now brought to the hospital after a sudden episode of seizures. On examination, his GCS is 13/15 and there is a rash on his lower extremities. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, a single episode of seizures, and altered consciousness since this morning. On examination, the GCS is 7/15, signs of meningeal irritation (Brudzinski/Kernig) are positive, and there is a prominent purpuric rash on the legs and back. What is the most likely diagnosis?

There is no evidence of spasticity or hyperreflexia. Which of the following is the most likely site of the lesion?

A 3-month-old infant is brought to the clinic because he frequently "spits up" or regurgitates small amounts of milk shortly after feeding. answers.option: Positioning the baby upright after feeds and reassurance
Immediate change to an amino-acid-based formula

answers.option: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

question: A child is brought to the emergency department in severe respiratory distress. answers.option: Take blood pressure in the right leg only
Order an immediate CT scan of the head
Take pulses and blood pressure in all four limbs

answers.option: Hematuria, petechiae, and acute renal failure

Perform a thorough neurological examination and plot on growth chart over time
Immediately check for papilledema with fundoscopy

question: A 3-year-old child, who is fully vaccinated according to the national schedule, falls while playing and sustains a minor superficial cut on the knee and a small scratch on the hand. The wounds are clean. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

Administer tetanus toxoid now and a booster in 4 weeks

answers.option: Switch her to a different class of oral retinoids
Perform emergency neurosurgery to decompress the cerebral edema
